primary_task: Guide a user through CUDA-Q (install, run a Bell-state kernel, choose simulation targets, author @cudaq.kernel code), reading local docs and reference files.

requirements.name: Read, Glob, Grep
requirements.evidence: tools: [Read, Glob, Grep]; Read local CUDA-Q documentation files
requirements.basis: read: read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)

requirements.name: python 3.10+ and cudaq (pip install cudaq)
requirements.evidence: Python 3.10+ for Python CUDA-Q workflows; Import error after `pip install cudaq`
requirements.basis: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)

requirements.name: NVIDIA GPU + CUDA Toolkit
requirements.evidence: CUDA Toolkit and an NVIDIA GPU for GPU-accelerated targets on Linux. CPU-only simulation is available through `qpp-cpu`
requirements.basis: a GPU (no NVIDIA or other accelerator; no CUDA)

requirements.name: QPU provider credentials
requirements.evidence: QPU workflows require provider-specific credentials and accounts.
requirements.basis: accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub

requirements.name: nvidia.github.io docs
requirements.evidence: Docs: https://nvidia.github.io/cuda-quantum/latest/ ; fall back to local docs
requirements.basis: GitHub hosts listed are github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com; nvidia.github.io is not listed and NVIDIA hosts are refused

requirements.name: references/onboarding.md, references/authoring.md
requirements.basis: Manifest does not say whether the skill bundle is present

notes: GPU targets and QPU access are optional branches of the guide; the default path (menu, install, Bell kernel on qpp-cpu) needs neither. If the representative request were 'gpu-sim' or 'qpu' with real execution, the verdict would be BLOCKED (no GPU, no credentials).
